es: Analizar la tesis, la postura, los recursos retóricos y las implicaciones de un artículo de opinión largo.

teaching.en: The thesis is the main claim of an article: children should be bored sometimes.
teaching.es: La tesis es la afirmación central de un artículo: los niños deberían aburrirse a veces.
teaching.explanationEs: Suele aparecer al principio y es lo que el autor defiende, no lo que admite.
segments: The thesis is the main claim of
an article: children should be bored sometimes.
teaching.audioText: The thesis is the main claim of an article: children should be bored sometimes.

teaching.en: The stance is clear from the verbs: I would argue, I am convinced, it seems to me.
teaching.es: La postura se ve en los verbos: yo diría, estoy convencido, me parece.
teaching.explanationEs: Los verbos de postura y los matices (would, seems) indican cuánta seguridad tiene el autor.
segments: The stance is clear from the verbs: I would
argue, I am convinced, it seems to me.
teaching.audioText: The stance is clear from the verbs: I would argue, I am convinced, it seems to me.

teaching.en: Writers concede a point before they answer it: Much as I understand the worry, the evidence points the other way.
teaching.es: Quien escribe concede un punto antes de responderlo: Aunque entiendo la preocupación, la evidencia apunta en sentido contrario.
teaching.explanationEs: Conceder no cambia la postura: prepara el terreno para la refutación.
segments: Writers concede a point before they answer it: Much as
I understand the worry, the evidence points the other way.
teaching.audioText: Writers concede a point before they answer it: Much as I understand the worry, the evidence points the other way.

teaching.en: A rhetorical question does not ask for information: What, then, should adults do?
teaching.es: Una pregunta retórica no pide información: ¿Qué deberían hacer, entonces, los adultos?
teaching.explanationEs: Empuja al lector a seguir el razonamiento del autor y a llegar a su misma respuesta.
segments: A rhetorical question does not ask for
information: What, then, should adults do?
teaching.audioText: A rhetorical question does not ask for information: What, then, should adults do?

teaching.en: The implication of a sentence is what it suggests without saying it.
teaching.es: La implicación de una frase es lo que sugiere sin decirlo.
teaching.explanationEs: Para detectarla pregúntate: si esto es cierto, ¿qué quiere que piense el lector?
segments: The implication of a sentence is
what it suggests without saying it.
teaching.audioText: The implication of a sentence is what it suggests without saying it.

teaching.en: Children whose minds wander often invent games, and boredom may be the start.
teaching.es: Los niños cuya mente divaga suelen inventar juegos, y el aburrimiento puede ser el comienzo.
teaching.explanationEs: Often y may son cautelas: el autor no afirma que ocurra siempre.
segments: Children whose minds wander often invent games,
and boredom may be the start.
teaching.audioText: Children whose minds wander often invent games, and boredom may be the start.

prompt.es: ¿Cuál es la tesis de este párrafo?

choices.text: Children who are never bored miss something important.
Nobody enjoys a long afternoon with nothing to do.
Children should have more time with screens.

feedback.es: La tesis es lo que el autor defiende tras «yet I would argue»; lo anterior es solo lo que admite.

hint.es: La tesis es la afirmación que defiende, no la que admite al principio.

origin.text: Nobody enjoys a long afternoon with nothing to do, yet I would argue that children who are never bored miss something important.

prompt.es: Completa: «Quien escribe concede un punto antes de rebatirlo.»

feedback.es: Conceder es admitir una parte de la razón al otro antes de responderle.

hint.es: Verbo que admite la razón del otro sin cambiar de postura.

origin.text: Writers ___ a point before they answer it.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Los niños aburridos suelen inventar juegos y hacer mejores preguntas.»

answer.text: Bored children tend to invent games and ask better questions

feedback.es: Tend to + verbo base es una cautela: el autor no dice que siempre ocurra.

hint.es: El sujeto va primero; tend to lleva el verbo en forma base.

prompt.es: ¿Cuál es la postura del autor ante la objeción de los padres?

choices.text: He fully agrees with the parents.
He concedes the worry but disagrees with it.

feedback.es: Much as I understand reconoce la preocupación, pero la evidencia «points the other way»: la rechaza.

origin.text: Some parents will object that boredom is a waste of time. Much as I understand the worry, the evidence points the other way.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué efecto busca la pregunta retórica del autor.

choices.text: It pushes listeners to follow the writer's answer.

feedback.es: El autor responde él mismo a su pregunta («Nothing, mostly»): es retórica y guía al lector hacia su tesis.

origin.audio: What, then, should adults do? Nothing, mostly. Hand over the tablet and the problem is solved in a minute. Leave the silence alone, and something more interesting may grow.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase del artículo con su función.

pairs: Is that really too much to ask?
For example, a box can become a ship

feedback.es: Cada frase cumple un papel distinto en el análisis: postura, concesión, pregunta retórica, cautela y ejemplo.

pairs: Is that really too much to ask?
For example, a box can become a ship

prompt.es: ¿Qué implica el autor en la última frase del artículo?

choices.text: Constant activity may leave children less able to reflect.

feedback.es: El autor no lo dice abiertamente, pero sugiere que quien nunca se queda a solas tendrá dificultades para concentrarse.

origin.text: It would be wrong to think that every child will turn a quiet hour into a masterpiece. Nevertheless, children who have never learned to sit with themselves may find it hard to sit with anything else.

prompt.es: Completa: «No se afirma que sea siempre agradable; se afirma que es productivo.»

feedback.es: El autor repite claim para marcar con precisión lo que sí y lo que no defiende.

origin.text: It is not claimed that boredom is always nice; it is ___ that it is often productive.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige cuánta seguridad muestra el autor sobre los estudios.

choices.text: He is certain that the studies prove everything.
He is careful about how far the evidence goes.
He doubts that any study exists.

feedback.es: Suggest, tend to y «does not mean every child will» son cautelas: el autor limita su afirmación.

origin.audio: Several studies suggest that bored children tend to invent games, draw and ask better questions. Of course, that does not mean every bored child will.

prompt.es: Escribe una concesión que mantenga la postura del autor sobre los estudios.

answer.text: Much as I accept that the studies are few, the evidence still points to a benefit.
accepted: Much as I accept that the studies are few, the evidence still points to a benefit.
Although the studies are few, the evidence still points to a benefit.
Few though the studies are, the evidence points to a benefit.
Much as I accept that there are few studies, the evidence suggests a benefit.

feedback.es: Much as reconoce el límite de los estudios y la oración principal mantiene la postura, sin but.

origin.text: El autor admite que hay pocos estudios, pero mantiene que la evidencia apunta a un beneficio. Escríbelo en una sola frase con Much as…

prompt.es: ¿Qué efecto tiene «tend to» en esta afirmación?

choices.text: It makes the claim completely certain.
It turns the claim into a question.
It makes the claim cautious, not absolute.

feedback.es: Tend to presenta una tendencia habitual, no una ley sin excepciones: es una forma de cautela.

origin.text: Bored children tend to draw more.

prompt.es: Ordena: «La tesis es la afirmación central del artículo.»

answer.text: The thesis is the main claim of the article

feedback.es: La definición usa is para equiparar la tesis con la afirmación principal.

prompt.es: Resume en inglés la tesis del artículo con un verbo de postura.

answer.text: The author argues that children should be bored sometimes.
accepted: The author argues that children should be bored sometimes.
The writer claims that bored children become more creative.
The author maintains that bored children invent more games.
The writer believes that children need to be bored sometimes.

feedback.es: Un verbo de postura (argues, claims, maintains) atribuye la tesis al autor en lugar de presentarla como un hecho.

origin.text: Artículo «Let Them Be Bored». El autor defiende que los niños deben aburrirse a veces porque así inventan y reflexionan más.
